findings.quote: can be given by you to whomever you wish.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna here: ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν οἷς ἂν βούλησθε * / ** προστεθέντα. The infinitive governing the list (Lycaonia, Hellespontine Phrygia, Pisidia, Chersonese) and the connection to προστεθέντα are lost; the English reads on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: can be given by you to whomever you wish [gap in the Greek text here].

units.note: The Greek chapter ends mid-sentence (οὐδεμιᾶς ἂν γένοιτο); the English completes it with 'inferior to no other monarchy' from the opening of ch. 23 (τῶν ἄλλων δυναστειῶν καταδεεστέρα). That is a chapter-seam matter, not an error.

findings.quote: while those that had paid tribute to Antiochus alone should have that tribute remitted.
findings.problem: Greek: ὅσαι δ᾽ Ἀντιόχῳ, μόνον ταύταις ἀφεῖσθαι τὸν φόρον. μόνον goes with ταύταις: only the cities that had paid Antiochus are released from tribute. English 'Antiochus alone' reads as cities that paid no one but Antiochus, which shifts the sense.
findings.proposed_fix: while only those that had paid tribute to Antiochus should have that tribute remitted.

findings.problem: Greek: οἵ τε περὶ τὸν Σκιπίωνα καὶ Λεύκιον — singular Σκιπίωνα, i.e. Scipio and his party (the earlier τοὺς περὶ τὸν Σκιπίωνα is rendered 'Scipio' in the same chapter), plus Lucius (apparently Aemilius Regillus, the naval victor). 'The Scipios' makes the name plural and changes who arrives.
findings.proposed_fix: Scipio and his party, and Lucius

units.note: The plural participle οἱ ... νικήσαντες covers both Scipio's party and Lucius; the identification of Lucius is not given in the Greek here, so the English should not specify it.

findings.problem: Greek: τὰ περὶ τοὺς Ἀθαμᾶνας καὶ τὴν τοῦ Φιλίππου *** — there is a lacuna after τοῦ Φιλίππου. 'weakness there' is supplied, not in the Greek.
findings.proposed_fix: and Philip’s [gap in the Greek text]

units.note: Sibyrtus τοῦ Πετραίου: 'son of Petraeus' versus 'of Petra' is uncertain from the Greek alone; left unflagged.

findings.quote: These broke through the enemy entrenchment lying between and slipped into the city.
findings.problem: Greek: εἰσέφρησαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, * / ** παραγγείλας — the genitive absolute about Nicander has no main verb, and a lacuna follows. English reads on as if complete.
findings.proposed_fix: These broke through the enemy entrenchment lying between and slipped into the city. [gap in the Greek text]

findings.quote: He had instructed them that on the agreed day they were to sally out, while he himself would join in and support the danger.
findings.problem: Greek: αὐτοὺς μὲν ἐξελθόντας *** ποιήσασθαι — a lacuna after ἐξελθόντας; the object of ποιήσασθαι is missing. The subject of παραγγείλας also stands after a lacuna.
findings.proposed_fix: [Nicander] having instructed them that on the agreed day they were to sally out and [gap in the Greek text], while he himself would join them in the danger.

findings.quote: They rushed boldly out of the city and fought gallantly
findings.problem: Greek begins *** αὐτῶν μὲν εὐψύχως τῆς πόλεως ἐξορμησάντων — a lacuna precedes this clause; English begins as if continuous.
findings.proposed_fix: [gap in the Greek text] When they rushed boldly out of the city and fought gallantly

findings.problem: Greek: στύπη δρύινα, 'oak logs/stumps'. 'Wrapped in tow' has no counterpart in the Greek.

units.note: Three lacunae in the Greek of this chapter; the English reads on smoothly across all of them.
